excerpt_i18n.en:
Top News Briefs:
1. Insiders refuted the rumor of "Midea being fined 5 million yuan by JD.com" as fabricated, suggesting clear platform manipulation.
2. Xiaomi undergoes intensive restructuring: Lei Ming personally leads the new automotive division, while Chen Kai takes over Xiaomi Stores.
3. Zhong Shanshan tops China's rich list for the fourth time with a fortune of 530 billion yuan, and Xiaomi's Lei Jun becomes the "growth king."
4. MiniMax's senior research director Zhong Yiran left the company six months ago.
5. Giant Network's CEO Zhang Dong resigns, with board member Liu Wei appointed as the new CEO.
6. Meta's AI division undergoes major layoffs: Llama4's loss to Chinese competitors leads to strategic restructuring.
7. With a 30% commission rate yielding high profits, Apple's services revenue is expected to surpass $100 billion for the first time.

Today's Headlines:
Insiders have responded to the rumor of "Midea being fined 5 million yuan by JD.com" as fabricated, indicating clear signs of platform manipulation. Recently, a series of messages about JD.com enforcing strict pricing policies on merchants during the Double 11 shopping festival circulated on social platforms, including screenshots claiming "Midea Group was fined 5 million yuan by JD.com over pricing issues." On October 28, media sources close to both Midea and JD.com confirmed this as false information. The insiders noted that a concentrated wave of media and self-media outlets spreading such rumors, along with false claims about JD.com's "choose one" policy, shows evident signs of platform manipulation. It is reported that numerous videos and screenshots on platforms like Douyin have recently emerged, accusing JD.com of aggressive pricing tactics toward merchants during Double 11, with many accounts alleging JD.com's "choose one" approach. JD.com's customer service had earlier clarified that they had not received any related reports of "choose one."
excerpt_i18n.es: Resumen de noticias clave: 1. Fuentes informadas responden que el caso "Midea multada con 5 millones por JD.com" es un rumor, con evidencia de manipulación por parte de la plataforma. 2. Ajustes intensivos en Xiaomi: Lei Jun asume personalmente el nuevo departamento de automóviles, mientras Chen Kai toma el relevo en Xiaomi Home. 3. Zhong Shanshan, con un patrimonio de 530.000 millones de yuanes, se convierte por cuarta vez en el hombre más rico de China, y Lei Jun de Xiaomi es el "rey del crecimiento". 4. Zhong Yiran, directora senior de investigación de MiniMax, dejó su cargo hace medio año. 5. Zhang Dong, CEO de Giant Network, renuncia, y Liu Wei, directora de la empresa, asume como CEO. 6. Grandes despidos en el departamento de IA de Meta: la derrota de Llama4 ante competidores chinos lleva a una reestructuración estratégica. 7. El 30% de comisión genera altos beneficios, y se espera que los ingresos anuales por servicios de Apple superen por primera vez los 100.000 millones de dólares.

excerpt_i18n.en: Lei Feng Network AI Tech Review exclusively learned that MiniMax's Senior Research Director, Zhong Yiran, has left the company, with her next destination not yet publicly disclosed. Public records show Dr. Zhong Yiran earned her Ph.D. from the Australian National University under the supervision of Professor Li Hongdong and Academician Richard Hartley. She has published over 40 research papers in internationally recognized journals and top-tier academic conferences, including TPAMI, IJCV, IEEE TIP, CVPR, NeurIPS, ECCV, ICCV, ICLR, and EMNLP, and holds multiple U.S. patents. She also received the 2023 ICCV Workshop Best Paper Award and the 2014 ICIP Best Student Paper Award. After completing her Ph.D., Zhong Yiran joined SenseTime in 2021 as a Senior Manager, focusing on research in large language models, multi-turn dialogue, and multimodal fusion. By the end of 2023, at MiniMax, she proposed concepts for efficient architectures in large models and collaborated with the R&D team to advance linear attention mechanisms in large-scale language models.

AI is no longer a standalone algorithm but has become the decision-making engine of IoT systems. The new goal for AIoT computing networks and agent systems is to imbue the physical world with cognitive and autonomous capabilities akin to a nervous system. At the 2025 World Laureates Forum, Kevin Yin, founder and CEO of Terminus Group, was invited to share insights with top global tech leaders on advancing the large-scale implementation of advanced AI technologies and launched a series of AIoT products, including "Heterogeneous Computing Super Nodes" and "New Intelligent Agents." 

Redefining AIoT: From Hybrid Intelligence Computing to Super Intelligent Agents

At the forum, Kevin Yin officially unveiled Terminus Group's upgraded corporate strategy, focusing on AIoT technology with computing power (AIoT Infra) and intelligent agents (AIoT Agent) as the two core business areas to accelerate the widespread adoption of AI. Computing power serves as the foundational support, providing high-performance computational resources for top-level intelligent agents, while the agents enhance the utilization and energy efficiency of cluster resources through their "perception-decision-execution" closed loop, fostering iterative improvements in computing infrastructure and creating a positive feedback cycle.

Kevin Yin also detailed the product architecture and model of Terminus Group's computing power (AIoT Infra) business, which utilizes a cluster of heterogeneous chip hardware and two software platforms—the spatial intelligence base TacOS and the hybrid inference engine HICE—to build a hybrid intelligence computing cloud. This setup offers standardized, stable inference services and computing power leasing operations to the industry, establishing a TaaS (Token as a Service) business model.
excerpt_i18n.es: La IA ya no es un algoritmo aislado, sino el motor de decisión de los sistemas IoT. Dotar al mundo físico de capacidades cognitivas y autónomas similares a un sistema nervioso se ha convertido en el nuevo objetivo de las redes de computación AIoT y los sistemas de agentes inteligentes. En el Foro Mundial de Científicos Líderes 2025, Ai Yu, fundador y CEO de Telstra, fue invitado a compartir logros exploratorios en la implementación a gran escala de tecnologías avanzadas de IA junto con líderes globales de la tecnología, y presentó productos de la serie AIoT como "nodos superiores de computación heterogénea" y "nuevos agentes inteligentes". Redefiniendo AIoT: de la computación inteligente híbrida al superagente inteligente. Durante el foro, Ai Yu lanzó oficialmente la estrategia empresarial actualizada de Telstra, centrada en AIoT.

excerpt_i18n.en: A few days ago, an experiment called the "AI Trading Battle" went viral on overseas social media. The organizers gave six major models, including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, $10,000 in virtual funds each to freely trade cryptocurrencies. The results were surprising: as of today, DeepSeek V3.1 achieved an astonishing profit rate of over 126%, while GPT 5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro dropped below $5,000, with loss rates exceeding 50%. This "AI trading show" was originally intended to showcase the financial potential of intelligence but instead revealed a deeper issue: when faced with complex and dynamic financial environments, do language models understand why they place orders? A recent paper by a joint research team from Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Rutgers University in the U.S., and Nankai University provides an answer to such questions. They proposed a method called RETuning, which enables large language models to gather evidence, analyze logic, reflect on reasoning, and then draw conclusions before making predictions. In other words, the models no longer rely on intuitive judgments but have learned to think with justification. The research team systematically validated this method using a large-scale dataset covering China's A-share market. The results show that RETuning not only significantly improves prediction accuracy but also makes the model's reasoning process clearer and more credible.
excerpt_i18n.es: Hace unos días, un experimento llamado "Batalla de Comercio con IA" se volvió viral en redes sociales internacionales. Los organizadores asignaron diez mil dólares virtuales a cada uno de seis modelos principales, incluyendo ChatGPT, Gemini y Claude, para que operaran libremente en el mercado de criptomonedas. Los resultados fueron sorprendentes: hasta hoy, DeepSeek V3.1 logró una rentabilidad impresionante superior al 126%, mientras que GPT 5 y Gemini 2.5 Pro cayeron por debajo de los 5.000 dólares, con pérdidas que superan el 50%. Este "espectáculo de comercio con IA" originalmente buscaba demostrar la inteligencia.
